Subject: Post-demo: grounding strategy, retrieval & reranker proposal for Nimbus Health

Hi Susan (and team) —

Thanks again for the demo time this morning. Quick recap and the proposal for next steps so we keep momentum:

What we heard from Nimbus:
- Primary goal: reliable, auditable grounding for patient-facing Q&A inside the Nimbus portal.
- Success metrics: factuality/grounding precision > 92% on the clinical FAQ set, average latency < 250ms tail for interactive flows, and privacy controls aligned with their SOC2/policy needs.

Redwood proposal (high level):
1) Retriever config: hybrid vector + sparse (BM25) with a conservative recall window (top-k=50, reranker pre-filter top-50 -> rerank top-5). We recommend using compressed vector index with 512-d floats quantized for latency.
2) Reranker: pairwise transformer reranker (fine-tuned on Nimbus dev set) to prioritize provenance-rich passages. Start with our v2 reranker config (see attachment).
3) Models & evals: run parallel A/B of two model families for fit — a 7B quantized LLM for low-latency paths and a 13B finetuned variant for high-accuracy routes. We’ll instrument evals with the prompt set you shared plus expanded adversarial prompts.
4) Monitoring & regression: set rolling quality checks on the prompt set (daily sampling), and alert on 3%+ drop in grounding precision.

Attachments I’ll share: candidate benchmark CSV, prompt set snapshot, and the reranker config prototype.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Redwood to deliver initial baseline benchmarks (system-level retrieval+reranker) by Wed 3/3 EOD.
- Nimbus to confirm the representative prompt subset (ideally 250 items) and a small holdout (50 items) for blind eval.
- Set a 30-minute follow-up to review numbers and pick the production path (tune retriever vs. upgrade reranker).

Can you confirm the prompt subset timeline and availability for a follow-up on Thurs (3/4)?

Thanks,
Vivek

Hi Susan — quick technical answers, and I've attached the baseline bench CSV and the eval notebook.

Reranker latency: our measured P95 for pairwise transformer reranker when ranking 50 candidates on a p3-like instance (optimized kernels) is ~95–130ms depending on sequence length. For short passages (<= 128 tokens) expect ~100ms P95. If 120ms is a hard requirement, we can:
- Option A: pre-filter with a lightweight lexical scorer (BM25) and only rerank top-20 (reduces P95 to ~70–80ms).
- Option B: use an optimized distilled reranker model (v2-lite) with ~45–60ms P95 but ~2–3% drop in ranking quality on our clinical validation set.

Model accuracy tradeoffs: on an internal clinical entity grounding benchmark (approx 2k queries):
- 7B quantized: grounding precision 88.8%
- 13B finetuned: grounding precision 93.6%
The 13B helps with longer-context disambiguation and rare entity recall. Quantization on the 7B is conservative; switching to a lightly finetuned 7B improves to ~90.5% at modest cost.

Data retention: vectors are optional and configurable per-client. By default Redwood stores vectors for 30 days and allows TTL or immediate purge via API. We can provide a SOC2-friendly data-retention addendum and an HSM/KMS integration to control keys.

Attachments: nimbus_rag_benchmarks.csv, eval-notebook.ipynb (link inside), reranker-config-v2.yaml, prompt-library-v1.jsonl.

-- Marcus
